chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who has two wives, and one of them said, 'My night and day are for you for a day or a month or whatever it is.' Is that permissible? He said, 'If she is pleased with it and he purchases it from her, there is no harm.'

key_terms.طَابَتْ نَفْسُهَا: She was pleased/content (her soul was pleased)
key_terms.لَيْلَتِي وَيَوْمِي: My night and day (dedication of time)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a wife to dedicate her time to her husband for a specific period in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the permissibility of a wife dedicating her conjugal time to her husband for a fixed duration is established, provided there is mutual consent and a form of compensation ('shara') is agreed upon. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'ibrah' (mutual agreement) in marital relations, allowing flexibility in rights beyond the obligatory nightly visitation. The condition of 'tayyib nafsa' (pleased soul) underscores the importance of the wife's voluntary satisfaction rather than mere legal validity.
